open_points.subject: PortRef variants used by capture
open_points.text: “The functions capability keeps the broad PortRef input contract.” Neither PortRef, FileFactsRef, StoredValuesRef nor SpooledFilesRef is defined in the accepted models, while M23 says a NodeExecution names SpooledFiles “by their facts.”
open_points.question: What exact semantic fact distinguishes a refused FileFactsRef from a readable SpooledFilesRef, especially for a many-file port whose list is empty?
options: A SpooledFilesRef carries the full M22 run/producer/attempt/port/list-position identity, while a FileFactsRef carries only digest, size and media type.
Any reference represented only by file facts is a FileFactsRef, which would also classify M23 file inputs as facts-only.
The reference has an explicit variant tag, including for an empty list, independent of the fields it contains.
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit per-port variant tag; a SpooledFilesRef includes the full M22 identities needed to locate bytes, while FileFactsRef contains non-locating facts only.

open_points.subject: Inputs captured from a NodeExecution
open_points.text: M06 and A15 say the failed execution’s inputs “become the case’s inputs” and that capture “copies its inputs,” but the change describes a callable receiving and checking a “complete input tuple” without saying that the tuple must equal the selected NodeExecution’s recorded inputs.
open_points.question: Must the supplied PortRef tuple be derived from, or checked for exact equality with, the captured NodeExecution’s inputs, and which layer verifies that invariant?
options: The capture operation derives the tuple from the NodeExecution; callers cannot supply alternatives.
The caller supplies the tuple, and the capture caller verifies exact per-port equality with the NodeExecution before calling the functions capability.
The functions capability verifies the supplied tuple against the NodeExecution.
Any fitting tuple is accepted even if it was not the failed execution’s input.
open_points.default_guess: Require the capture caller to verify exact per-port equality with the NodeExecution, then pass those references to the functions capability.

open_points.subject: Executed implementation resolution during capture
open_points.text: “The callable first resolves the executed implementation… An unknown implementation remains unknown_reference.” A capture is selected by a NodeExecution, whose executed implementation is durable and cannot be deleted under A01 rule 6, so the text does not identify how an unknown executed implementation can be supplied or observed.
open_points.question: Where does the implementation identity being resolved come from, and if the caller supplies it separately, must it equal the implementation named by the captured NodeExecution?
options: It is always read from NodeExecution.executed; an unknown implementation indicates corrupt stored data and is not a surface refusal.
The request or capture caller supplies it, and it must equal NodeExecution.executed.
The request or caller supplies it, with no comparison to NodeExecution.executed.
open_points.default_guess: Read it from NodeExecution.executed; if an internal callable also receives the identity, require equality with that field.

open_points.subject: Unknown input references versus FileFactsRef refusal
open_points.text: The change says its order is “after the external request checks of A16” and also checks for FileFactsRef “before looking up any input value or spooled file.” A16 rule 1 says a request directly naming any nonexistent record is refused as unknown_reference before the operation’s own checks.
open_points.question: For a capture tuple containing both a FileFactsRef and an unknown StoredValue or SpooledFile reference, which refusal wins, and may the kernel look up that unknown reference before the FileFactsRef scan?
options: A16 wins: resolve every directly named reference first and return unknown_reference.
The new FileFactsRef scan wins and performs no input-reference lookup.
PortRefs are not records named directly for A16, so only the executed implementation and named contract version receive A16 unknown-reference checks.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the new explicit scan as winning for nested input PortRefs: refuse the first FileFactsRef without looking up any input reference.

open_points.subject: FileFactsRef check relative to existing input validation
open_points.text: A04 rule 1 orders captured-case input failures by port name and then “presence, carriage, schema, then size,” while the change says, “Next it checks the complete input tuple for facts-only file references” and that readable references “continue through the existing fit, size and copy checks.” It does not say whether non-lookup structural failures precede the FileFactsRef scan.
open_points.question: If the tuple both contains a FileFactsRef and is missing a port, has an extra port, or has a wrong-carriage reference, which condition is reported first?
options: Scan all supplied ports for FileFactsRef before every presence, carriage, schema and size check.
Perform presence and tuple-shape checks first, then scan for FileFactsRef before resolving references.
Keep A04 rule 1’s port-by-port presence, carriage, schema and size order, encountering FileFactsRef as a carriage failure at its port.
open_points.default_guess: Perform the categorical FileFactsRef scan immediately after the implementation/version checks, before all existing fit, size and copy checks.
